cards.title: Working Parents Face School Holiday Logistics Nightmare
cards.body: School holidays create a scheduling crisis for working parents juggling childcare and work commitments. Emily Mulligan argues we should celebrate school breaks as time to connect with kids rather than viewing them as disruptions.

cards.title: Halloween Magic: Ditching Cynicism for Family Connection
cards.body: Iman Amrani embraces Halloween celebrations as a moment of wonder and connection with her children. Ancient autumn traditions offer opportunities to create meaningful family memories beyond commercial expectations.

cards.title: AI Is Changing How Children Learn, Parents Must Pay Attention
cards.body: Children need opportunities to struggle, make mistakes, and figure things out—this is how genuine learning happens. Parents should understand AI's impact on their kids' educational development and critical thinking skills.

cards.title: Never Diagnose Someone Else's Child With Neurodivergence
cards.body: It's not your place to label or diagnose another person's child, even with good intentions. Supporting neurodivergent children means staying in your lane while offering meaningful help to families.

cards.title: When Good Parents Have Unintended Regrets With Children
cards.body: Parents can acknowledge that loving intentions sometimes cause unintended pain to their children. Recognition and empathy transform regret into deeper understanding rather than self-condemnation.

cards.title: Allergy Management Ratings Needed After Girl's Death
cards.body: Twelve-year-old Mia St Hilaire died from anaphylactic shock after drinking a milkshake containing tree nuts she was allergic to. Her death highlights the urgent need for better allergy management standards and ratings.

cards.title: NHS Blamed for Baby's Death, Pushes System Change
cards.body: Neil and Katie Russell are working with the hospital where their daughter died to implement meaningful reforms. Their advocacy aims to prevent similar tragedies and improve NHS accountability.

cards.title: Active Listening Skills Build Stronger Family Friendships
cards.body: Quality relationships develop through demonstrating genuine interest by asking thoughtful questions and showing empathy. Active listening with awareness and understanding strengthens bonds between family members and friends.
